prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1095; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a side impact at an intersection this morning. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.
Entry 2: Spoke with the other driver, who described the collision the same way the claimant did, including which vehicle entered the intersection first.
Entry 3: The police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Scene photos line up with the described sequence.
Entry 4: Reviewed damage to the claimant's vehicle. It is largely in line with a side impact at the angle described, and I see no sign of older damage in the same areas.
Entry 5: Claimant reports neck pain consistent with whiplash, and the force of the collision looks like a reasonable match for that kind of injury. No earlier injury to the neck or shoulder is known.
Entry 6: Claimant has given the same account in every call and meeting so far, including the order of events and what happened immediately afterward.
Entry 7: Treatment records show visits have grown to near-daily, many times the usual amount for this injury, with new body areas added several weeks after the collision. This needs a closer look.
Entry 8: Confirmed the driver of the claimant's vehicle lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy.
Entry 9: Verified the policy was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.
Entry 10: Referred the medical file to our nurse reviewer to compare the treatment against the injury and crash forces. Will follow up with the attorney's office on the outstanding records request.
